summary: v24/v20 preserve the repaired Pin/evidence closure, Linux FD/OFD boundary, child IPC and post-S5 continuation, but still leave three architecture-level normal-failure gaps: no deployable cross-identity P0/P1/archive-acceptor process graph, a path-only worker adapter incompatible with both its ACL and Python import-provenance model, and no durable canonical target for staged invocation/normalized-result evidence that archive recovery must re-open.

limitations: No product, test, contract, gate, ledger, status, or historical-evidence changes were made.
No project-code execution, training, archival replay, budget consumption, PIT certification, M7, or final-OOS access occurred.

blockers: Freeze a deployable outer-dispatcher actor-launch and S5-to-archive-acceptor handoff protocol, including UID/GID/capability transition, fixed helper/runtime binding, FD/socket allow-list, separate lease acquisition and crash behavior.
Freeze an executable legacy-worker adapter that reconciles resolved pathname ACLs with worker-job isolation and proves every imported qlib_peerlite module comes from the staged frozen inventory.

Define durable immutable persistence and archive-reopen semantics for StagedMechanicsInvocationV1 and NormalizedMechanicsResultV1; a job/scratch object cannot be an implicit long-term official dependency.
Resolve the m6_replay_fs SlotSpec upward-import contradiction through a lower-layer publication DTO/protocol before implementation.

Reissue architecture and change design, then obtain a new independent R3 design-review PASS before test design, implementation, code review, replay, M7, CCC/Gate, PIT certification, or final-OOS work.
